I tried over two years but it never stopped being more pain than it was worth. I'm glad some people feel relived by the intrusive structure of Workona, but I really regret investing time into adapting to the system.

And once I gave up on it, re-separating my tabs for a straightforward tab manager was a nightmare. 

Workona's worth a try if you're experimenting with with these extensions but if the frustrations don't end after the learning curve, don't throw good energy after bad if it keeps doing more harm than good in your workflow. All said, it never saved me any time/effort

reviews.text: Functional for 5 spaces. That's it. Before you would be able to archive spaces and add sections to the workspaces but it's locked behind a paywall. It's better to look for other alternatives!

I honestly love this extension. The only reason I gave 3 stars is because you can only have up to 5 work spaces before needing to purchase the premium for more space (which is actually a decent amount if you don't have a lot of of different topics or projects to be working on that need their separate space). For me, I am definitely going to need more space since the reason I started using workona was to get organized to start a remote job. However, purchasing the premium is NOT feasible. Essentials like this should be freely accessible with unlimited spaces. When you consider that $7 a month over a year accumulates to $84 solely for additional tab spaces, it's hard to see it as a justifiable expense.  It's disheartening to realize that even something as basic as a tab organization tool comes with a price tag. 

Despite this, the extension itself is necessary and very easy to use. I use it everyday. I hope that they consider my review and make it free for unlimited work spaces.

Workona is one of those special extensions you find that can do so much for you.  Unfortunately, for me personally, it's not stable enough.  It consistently loses tabs and they drop out of their Chrome Tab Groups.  This is a serious blocker as I usually have around 50 tabs across 3 workspaces open at once and without these two key functions, Workona is useless, I'll give it a few more weeks, then I'll cancel my subscription. :-(
tags: tabs drop out of chrome tab groups

reviews.text: Workona is great, used it for quite some time and even paid for it, but I hate the fact that it kind of takes over the natural functionality of chrome's tabs and chrom's new window management. It gets in my way, sort of. When I open a new window, sometimes the other one just closes, and I end up having to reopen everything. Annoying.    I also use the TabBrew, simple and effective automatic grouping by domain. It doesn't get in my way. It integrates nicely with Chrome's tab groups and doesn't try to do too much which could end up pushing people away (because using chrome could, of course, be enhanced by extensions but should still remain natural and intuitive)

reviews.text: I loved this tab manager for a while. However, now that they've implemented what I think is a steep pay wall ($9/month), most basic features like having anything more than 5 workspaces, restoring tabs, and sharing, renaming, or duplicating an existing workspace are unavailable for existing free users. If you can afford $9/month, it's great. I just can't justify spending that when there are so many other tab managers available.

Great for organizing my cluttered tabs. Before I had to sort all my tabs into groups. Now I can sort them into groups in categories. There is a five group limit, but I don't mind. I just prioritize four and have a miscellaneous one for everything else. I found it right before needing my computer more often, and it's helped a lot.

Very handy! Finally I have an easy way to have the tabs open that I need for a particular task or topic I want to work on. Easy to switch to something else by choosing the appropriate workspace.

An unexpected benefit is that I am more focused when I work on something as there are "only" the websites open that I need for that topic (each important topic now has its own Workona workspace). I have one workspace that is dedicated to temporary stuff, i.e. general webbrowsing etc. where I don't have a specific topic in mind, and unless that is the workspace I'm in when a random thought strikes me, I don't open a new tab. I am finding it easier to keep myself working on the topic I've chosen as my current focus now that I don't "quickly" open something else (which does tend to waste a lot of time...) by the simple expedient of not opening a new tab if it doesn't fit with the workspace I have open at the time.
Gud! Dumped Opera and switched to this

It's really good for managing your tabs well. However, there were a few things that I wish could be improved on. For one, there was a maximum of two spaces, and if I created another space, it would self delete once I exited it. Also, if you close the hidden tab window and try to go to that space, once you go there all the tabs are gone. Not sure if this is just a glitch on my part, but it was quite inconvenient. Great for separating your tabs though. I find the best way for me to use it is to create a separate space whenever I need to study online. As a student, it really helps to have a way to separate my more distracting tabs and make them not be there when I need to focus. Just like they say, out of sight, out of mind! In addition, if your a writer, and artist, or you have a hobby/job that requires you to often plan out projects, this is good for that as you can create a separate space for each project.
It's very helpful and great, but we you are in a google meet you have to go there manually and not press the "go to meet button" because it won't allow you to, but sill it is a good extension.

This has been really helpful, and I'm actually considering paying for the premium version (which I almost never do)- the free features have been great for getting me organized and now I want to go farther! It's pretty streamlined and easy to work with.
"I feel like the speed of switching to a new space is a bit slow; is there any way to optimize it?"

This software has made my life juggling multiple clients so much easier! The seamless switching between my client groups is such a time saver and no more randomly bookmarking tabs to come back to later. And the fact I can save all my resources within Workona as well such as Google drives is brilliant.

This extension is a great time-saver for organizing multiple tabs across different tasks like studying, job hunting, and entertainment. It keeps everything tidy and boosts productivity. Adding a feature to freeze specific tabs without saving their history would make it even better by improving privacy and control.

I was overwhelmed with having up to 7-10 instances of Chrome each with multiple tabs as a way to organize all my tabs by category, where each browser instance was a category of work, project, etc.  In each browser instance, it  became difficult to find the tab I wanted as they really can't be identified by the tab name.  Having that many browser instances was also dragging on memory.  Workona splendidly solved all that and gave me a way to organize work categories (now workspaces organized by sections in Workona) and a way to find my tab very quickly by organizing tabs into "Resources" each with its own subcategory name.  This allowed me to organize and find things much quicker given its hierarchical layout, similar to how I organize in OneNote with its hierarchical layout. 

I found Workona's GUI easy to use and intuitive and have found no bugs or issues as of yet.  Its now indispensable to me.
